title.big: Wind & current loads on a tanker, answered in chat
title.desc: Ask in plain English. Deckhand asks for what it needs, runs the calculation, and sends back a report you can keep.

turns.html: I need the wind and current loads on a moored VLCC — the surge and sway force and the yaw moment for a given heading. Can you screen it?

Happy to. A few details so I screen it the right way:
  • Tanker size and loading condition — give me length, beam, draft and displacement (or just tell me it's a loaded VLCC and I'll work from that).
  • Wind speed and the heading it's coming from.
  • Current speed and its heading.
I work this with the OCIMF wind- and current-coefficient method for tankers. Heading is measured off the bow, so 0° is head-on and 90° is on the beam.
Loaded VLCC — 330 m LOA, 60 m beam, 22 m draft, 250,000 t displacement. Wind 20 m/s coming from 60°, current 1.5 m/s from 30°. Details attached.

Got it — loaded VLCC, wind 20 m/s at 60° and current 1.5 m/s at 30°. Here's the plan: pull the OCIMF coefficients for each heading, work out the wind force on the above-water profile and the current force on the hull, then add them to get the total surge force, sway force and yaw moment on the vessel. Running it now…

Here's the load breakdown — longitudinal (surge), lateral (sway) and yaw moment:
SourceSurge FxSway FyYaw Mz
Wind (60°)74 kN665 kN58 MN·m
Current (30°)1,394 kN4,186 kN670 MN·m
Total1,468 kN4,851 kN728 MN·m
Current dominates — it carries about 86% of the sway force and the bulk of the yaw moment. The total sway load is roughly 4.85 MN, which is the number your mooring pattern has to hold.

report.title: OCIMF Tanker Load Screen
report.inputs:
Vessel
Loaded VLCC · LOA 330 m · beam 60 m · draft 22 m · displacement 250,000 t

Environment
Wind:    20.0 m/s from 60° · air density 1.225 kg/m³
Current: 1.5 m/s from 30° · water density 1025 kg/m³

Profile areas
Above-water frontal 600 m² · lateral 3,300 m² · submerged frontal 1,320 m² · lateral 7,260 m²
report.methodology:
1 · Look up the OCIMF wind and current coefficients (CX, CY, CM) for each heading off the bow.
2 · Wind force = ½ · air density · wind speed² · area · coefficient, on the above-water profile.
3 · Current force = ½ · water density · current speed² · area · coefficient, on the submerged hull.
4 · Yaw moment from the moment coefficient, referenced to length.
5 · Total surge, sway and yaw = wind + current, the loads the mooring has to react.
report.outputs:
SourceSurge FxSway FyYaw Mz
Wind (60°)74 kN665 kN58 MN·m
Current (30°)1,394 kN4,186 kN670 MN·m
Total1,468 kN4,851 kN728 MN·m
Verdict: Total environmental load on the vessel is 1,468 kN surge, 4,851 kN sway and 728 MN·m yaw. Current drives it — about 95% of the sway force and most of the yaw moment — so the mooring pattern sizing is governed by the current, not the wind.
